items.subsection: What is factual from the tweets
items.title: 10,000 agents
items.summary: An OpenAI-linked claim circulated that a Navier–Stokes “solution” involved about 10,000 agents working collaboratively @ eknight .

items.subsection: What is factual from the tweets
items.title: Navier–Stokes existence/singularity problem
items.summary: Public readers understood the claim as concerning the Navier–Stokes existence/singularity problem , one of the Millennium Prize Problems , though the exact theorem statement and proof scope are not supplied in the tweet set @LearnOpenCV .

items.subsection: Meta’s Muse Launch and the Personal-Agent Security Architecture
items.title: Meta launched Muse
items.summary: , a consumer-facing “personal AI agent” positioned as always-on, app-connected, browser-capable, and goal-oriented, with strong distribution through Meta properties and integrations @finkd , @alexandr_wang , @MetaNewsroom .

items.subsection: Meta’s Muse Launch and the Personal-Agent Security Architecture
items.title: Security architecture is the differentiator being pushed hardest.
items.summary: Meta’s team said each Muse runs in its own secure VM , actions are mediated by a separate Sentinel , secrets are never directly exposed to the agent, sensitive actions require approval, and there is a public bug bounty up to $300k @shengjia_zhao , @alexandr_wa…

items.subsection: Meta’s Muse Launch and the Personal-Agent Security Architecture
items.title: Early reception from practitioners was notably positive
items.summary: , especially on permissioning, secrets management, and consumer utility. Commentary from @matthuang , @signulll , and @lilyjclifford suggests Muse may be one of the first broadly legible personal-agent products where context and access , not raw model IQ, are…

items.subsection: OpenAI’s Image 2.5 Release and Astra Rollout
items.title: Astra availability widened materially.
items.summary: OpenAI said GPT-6 Astra is now fully rolled out to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in Codex and ChatGPT Work @OpenAI . Community demos showed strong practical computer-use performance: @theo reported Astra compiling and running Super Smash Bros.

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, Post-Training, and Serving Infrastructure
items.title: Harvey + Baseten’s M&A diligence work is one of the clearest model-harness co-optimization case studies.
items.summary: Their recursive language model (RLM) harness uses a root agent to search a data room, delegate to sub-agents for document review, and aggregate findings over corpora up to 80M tokens .

items.subsection: Agent Harnesses, Post-Training, and Serving Infrastructure
items.title: LangChain/deepagents shipped quality-of-life primitives for harness design
items.summary: , including subagent forking that passes supervisor context down to subagents, plus managed connections to abstract OAuth/token/consent flows for either agent-owned or user-owned identities @colifran_ , @hwchase17 , @caspar_br .

items.subsection: Inference and Systems: Sparse Attention, Agentic Serving, and Decode Megakernels
items.title: vLLM’s long-context serving work is notable.
items.summary: The project described Hybrid HiSparse for sparse-MLA models: KV stays on GPU while possible, then cold KV pages are offloaded to host memory , while a hot buffer serves the indexer.

items.subsection: Inference and Systems: Sparse Attention, Agentic Serving, and Decode Megakernels
items.title: vLLM also published a full-stack optimization pass for real-world agent traffic
items.summary: , benchmarked on AgentX . Key takeaways: pipeline parallelism helps cold long prompts but loses on warm short turns; decode context parallelism depends strongly on the model’s attention stack; and session-sticky routing can beat naive load balancing because wa…

items.subsection: Inference and Systems: Sparse Attention, Agentic Serving, and Decode Megakernels
items.title: Cohere introduced an open-source serving stack built around a “decode megakernel,”
items.summary: claiming up to 1.58× faster performance than vLLM on North Mini Code and 1.25×–1.41× end-to-end gains at higher batch sizes @cohere .

items.title: OpenAI says AI solved one of maths’ biggest problems
items.summary: OpenAI is claiming its unreleased AI model just solved Navier-Stokes, the 3rd most famous unsolved math problem in the world that’s been open for ~90 years. It's one of the 7 Millennium Prize Problems, with a $1 million bounty.

items.title: AI researchers are starting to quit over ‘out-of-control’ AI fears
items.summary: Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic after three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI and Anthropic, saying neither company is acting responsibly and they’re “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.”
